title: General Characterization of Support-Based Hypothesis Testing
summary: The source contrasts a one-query Deutsch-Jozsa case with a structured Simon case requiring order-n queries and leaves a general characterization of the pattern unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Develop a general characterization of hypothesis-testing problems in which each hypothesis restricts the support of a correlation state to a prescribed subset of $\mathbb{F}_2^n \times \mathbb{F}_2^m$. The characterization should account for the contrast between Deutsch--Jozsa, whose subsets are disjoint and permit a decision after one query, and Simon's algorithm, whose structured family of subsets requires $O(n)$ queries. Multi-hypothesis sequential probability ratio tests (MSPRT) are a potential tool for this characterization.

scope.domain: Quantum hypothesis testing and query complexity for correlation-state support families.
parameters: n and m: dimensions of the two binary vector spaces in the prescribed support subset
number of queries: resource used to distinguish the hypothesis families
scope.unresolved_remainder: Develop a general characterization of these support-based hypothesis-testing problems, potentially using multi-hypothesis sequential probability ratio tests (MSPRT).

citations.label: A Geometric Approach to Quantum Distinguishers

progress.summary: The source presents Deutsch-Jozsa and Simon's algorithm as instances of a common support-based hypothesis-testing pattern with different query requirements. It leaves a general characterization for future work and suggests MSPRT as a potential tool.
